data.gender_notes: Austine is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Roman family name 'Augustus', derived from the Latin word 'augere' meaning 'to increase'. In Greek, it is derived from the Greek word 'autos' meaning 'self'. The name has been used in both genders and has associations with strength, independence, and austerity. The name Austine carries the meaning “Little, Austere” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Austine usually hope their child will grow to embody little, austere and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Austine total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_english.name: Austine
in_english.long_meaning: The name Austine originates from Latin, specifically from the name 'Augustinus,' meaning 'great, magnificent.' It is associated with Saint Augustine of Hippo, a prominent Christian theologian and philosopher. The name symbolizes greatness, reverence, and spiritual magnificence.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Austin" was popularized in the English-speaking world due to the many saints and scholars bearing the name throughout history. The name was particularly favored by the early Christian Church, with St. Austyn (also known as St. Augustine) being one of the most well-known individuals. This great theologian, philosopher, and bishop is credited with founding Monasticism in the Western world and is considered one of the Doctors of the Church. His influence on Christian thought and culture has been vast, enduring, and continues to be felt today.
data.spiritual_significance: The name 'Austin', with its roots in the Latin words 'augere' and 'autos', signifies an individual of great inner strength and self-reliance. In the Christian tradition, the name inspires a sense of austerity and devotion to God. Austin is also a reminder of the need for personal growth and the striving towards a greater purity of heart and mind, as depicted in the story of St. Augustine's conversion. The name is therefore often chosen for those who seek to deepen their spiritual connection with God and live in a manner consistent with the Christian principles.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Austin: Stone of Divinity. A name signifying one who is steadfast in faith and devoted to the divine.
